title: AgentAML: anti-money-laundering files for small estate agencies before the EU rules of July 2027
summary: From 10 July 2027 the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation applies directly to estate and letting agents in every member state. Small agencies must keep a written risk assessment, policies, customer checks and records. AgentAML gives them a simple file per deal, ID and ownership checks, and a ready policy pack.
hook: "We are three brokers. We know we must do KYC, but our money-laundering routine is a Word file from 2019."
story:
**Erik owns a 5-person estate agency in Uppsala.** Swedish brokers already fall under money-laundering rules, and the supervisor (FMI) has just raised the sector's risk level to **high** after finding large knowledge gaps in agencies. Erik's routine is an old Word document, and buyer checks are a photo of an ID card in the deal folder.

When the EU regulation applies in **July 2027**, he must show a documented risk assessment, a named AML officer, customer due diligence on **both sides of each deal** (in many countries), checks of beneficial owners when a company buys, and refresh dates for each customer. He wants a tool that makes each deal's AML file as easy as the contract.
whyNow: The EU AML Regulation (AMLR) applies from 10 July 2027 with one rulebook for all member states, and AMLA is consulting on detailed technical standards in 2026. Supervisors are already tightening: in the UK, HMRC fined 170 estate agency businesses in six months of 2025, and Sweden's FMI raised the sector's risk rating to high.
evidence: The AMLR starts to apply to estate agents on 10 July 2027 [Schoenherr / Mondaq]
Letting intermediaries are covered for rents of at least €10,000 a month; sales agents with no minimum [AML Watcher]
Obliged estate agents will need to appoint AML officers and put risk assessments and CDD policies in writing [KPMG Germany]
Sweden's FMI thematic review found large knowledge gaps in broker firms; the sector risk was raised from "significant" to "high" [FMI / Fastighetsmäklarförbundet]
HMRC fined 170 UK estate agency businesses £835,842 between April and September 2025 [Property Industry Eye]
HMRC proposed raising the annual AML supervision fee from £300 to £400 per branch [The Negotiator]

solution.title: Policy pack
solution.text: a guided interview creates the agency-wide risk assessment, AML policy and officer appointment in plain language, ready for the supervisor.

solution.title: File per deal
solution.text: each sale or letting gets an AML file: parties, roles, source of funds questions and risk level.

solution.title: Customer checks
solution.text: send the buyer or seller a link for ID verification (via an EU eID/ID provider), PEP and sanctions screening, and company owner lookup.

solution.title: Risk and refresh
solution.text: rules set the risk level, ask for extra checks when needed and schedule refresh dates.

solution.title: Report and audit
solution.text: red-flag notes, a suspicious-activity checklist and a full audit trail exportable for inspections.
